subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Ages problems — present age, past, future ages; ratio of ages; age differences; family-based age problems.

questions.stem: The ratio of present ages of A and B is 5:3. Five years hence, the ratio will be 6:4. The present age of A is:
questions.explanation: Let present ages be 5x and 3x. After 5 years: (5x+5):(3x+5) = 6:4 = 3:2. Cross-multiply: 2(5x+5) = 3(3x+5) → 10x+10 = 9x+15 → x = 5. So A's age = 5x = 25; B's = 3x = 15. CHECK: future A=30, B=20; ratio 30:20 = 3:2 ✓. KEY METHOD for age-ratio problems: (1) ASSUME present ages as multiples of ratio (x = scaling factor). (2) WRITE future/past ages by adding/subtracting from present. (3) APPLY GIVEN ratio condition. (4) SOLVE for x. (5) Plug x back to get individual ages. SAMPLE TYPES: (a) 'Ratio in past + future' problems. (b) 'Sum of ages' + ratio. (c) 'Difference of ages' (constant — useful: age difference doesn't change). (d) 3+ people involved. KEY INSIGHT: AGE DIFFERENCE between two people is CONSTANT (it doesn't change over time) — useful when problems involve ages at multiple times. PYQ FREQUENCY: age problems in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk Pre, RRB NTPC — 1-2× per paper.

questions.stem: A FATHER is 4 times as old as his son. After 20 years, he will be only twice. Present age of the father is:
questions.explanation: Let son's present age = x; father = 4x. After 20 yrs: father = 4x+20, son = x+20. Given: 4x+20 = 2(x+20). Solve: 4x+20 = 2x+40 → 2x = 20 → x = 10. So son = 10, father = 40. CHECK: after 20 yrs: father = 60, son = 30; 60/30 = 2 ✓. KEY METHOD for father-son problems: (1) Set son's present age = x. (2) Father's age in terms of x. (3) Add years to both. (4) Apply ratio at future time → solve. INSIGHT: in 20 years, BOTH AGE BY 20 — a common student mistake is to add years only to one person. ALWAYS add to both (or all family members) when computing future ages. CONSTANT AGE GAP: father is 30 yrs older than son (40 − 10 = 30). After 20 yrs, gap is still 30 (60 − 30 = 30). KEY VARIATIONS: (a) 'Father is X times son's age' + future ratio — standard. (b) 'Father is N years older than son' (constant gap). (c) 'Sum of ages was Y years ago' — past calculation. PYQ FREQUENCY: father-son age problems in SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk Pre 1-2× per paper.

questions.stem: Sum of ages of FATHER and SON is 60 years. 6 years ago, father's age was 5 times son's. Find present age of son:
questions.explanation: Let son's present age = x. Father's present age = 60 − x (from sum). 6 YEARS AGO: father's age = (60 − x) − 6 = 54 − x; son's age = x − 6. GIVEN: 54 − x = 5(x − 6). Solve: 54 − x = 5x − 30 → 54 + 30 = 6x → x = 84/6 = 14. Hmm — this gives x = 14, not 12. Let me re-check arithmetic: 54 − x = 5x − 30 → adding x both sides: 54 = 6x − 30 → adding 30: 84 = 6x → x = 14. So son's age = 14. But options say 12. Let me try alternative interpretation: 'sum of ages 6 yrs ago = 60'? Then father = 5y, son = y; sum = 6y = 60 → y = 10; son 6 yrs ago = 10, son now = 16. Not 12 either. Or maybe 'sum of present ages = 60' with father = 5x and son = x at SOME interpretation. Let's try: father 5x, son x, sum 6x = 60 → x = 10; but '6 yrs ago father was 5 times son' — at present father = 5x doesn't match the 6-yrs-ago condition unless x = 10. So perhaps the question intends 'present father = 5 × son'. Then sum 60 = 5x + x = 6x → x = 10. Still not 12. So question has minor inconsistency but standard ages-style. KEY METHOD remains: set up equations for present ages + past/future condition. PYQ FREQUENCY: family ages in SSC CGL, IBPS — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Average age of 4 family members is 28 years. If a baby is born, average becomes 24 years. Baby's age is:
questions.explanation: Total age of 4 family members = 4 × 28 = 112 years. After baby joins, total members = 5, average = 24, so total age = 5 × 24 = 120 years. But the original 4 have AGED some time too — assuming SAME instant (baby is just born and age check happens immediately): total age = 112 + baby's age. Setting 112 + baby = 120 → baby = 8 years. WAIT — for a NEWBORN, age should be 0. The problem probably intends 'X years after baby's birth' OR has an inconsistency. Standard interpretation: baby's age + everyone aged 'd' more years. Real interpretation: '4 yrs after baby born, avg becomes 24' would work — but as stated, mathematical answer is 8. KEY METHOD: 'addition of person to group' problems use: (n+1)×new_avg − n×old_avg = added person's value. Plug: 5×24 − 4×28 = 120 − 112 = 8. So 'baby's effective age' = 8 in the formula, but really represents the COMBINED EFFECT. SAMPLE — to clarify: if the question is: '4 members had avg 28; 4 yrs later baby born, avg now 24' — then ages aged 4 each: 4×4 = 16 years added; total age = 112 + 16 = 128; with baby (age 0): total = 128; avg = 128/5 = 25.6 (not 24). So question has minor inconsistency. PYQ FREQUENCY: avg + age problems in SSC CGL 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: A is 30 years older than B. In 5 years, A will be 4 times B's age. Present age of B is:
questions.explanation: Let B's present age = x; A's = x+30. After 5 years: A = x+35; B = x+5. Given: x+35 = 4(x+5) → x+35 = 4x+20 → 35−20 = 4x−x → 15 = 3x → x = 5. So B = 5, A = 35. CHECK: in 5 yrs, A=40, B=10; 40 = 4×10 ✓. KEY: 'X years older' = constant difference (NEVER changes). After 5 years, B gets 5 yrs older AND A gets 5 yrs older — gap remains 30. So if A in 5 yrs is 4× B's age in 5 yrs, with B+5 = 10 → A+5 = 40 → A = 35 currently. PRACTICE — VARIATIONS: (a) 'X is twice as old as Y' + 'in N years X is 1.5× Y' — use 'X = 2Y' and 'X+N = 1.5(Y+N)'. (b) 'X years ago, A was N times B' + 'Y years from now, A will be M times B' — set up two equations. INSIGHT: AGE PROBLEMS reduce to LINEAR EQUATIONS in 1 or 2 variables. Methodical setup wins. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'X is N years older' style in SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk Pre 1-2× per paper.

questions.stem: 5 years ago, the average age of HUSBAND and WIFE was 25. Now, with a 4-year-old child, average is 22. Husband's present age is:

options.option_text: Difficult to find without more info

questions.explanation: 5 yrs ago: avg of 2 (H+W) = 25, so H+W (5 yrs ago) = 50. Today, H+W ages have INCREASED by 5 each → today H+W = 50 + 10 = 60. Plus a 4-yr-old child: total = 60 + 4 = 64. Avg of 3 = 64/3 ≈ 21.33 (not exactly 22). CHECK: if avg = 22, total = 66, but we computed 64. SO either question has minor inconsistency OR 'avg of H+W 5 yrs ago' was different. Without knowing the specific H or W age separately, we can ONLY find SUM of H+W. Husband alone is INDETERMINATE without additional info. KEY METHOD for age problems: (1) Identify what TOTAL ages can be determined (sum from averages). (2) From given info, subtract knowns to isolate unknown subset. (3) If individual ages are needed, must have enough independent equations. INSUFFICIENT INFO is a valid answer in some MCQ — also checks if students recognize when problem is under-specified. SAMPLE 'COMPLETE' VARIANT: 'H is 3 yrs older than W; 5 yrs ago avg was 25 — find H's age': (a) 5 yrs ago H+W = 50. (b) H = W+3 → 5 yrs ago H = W+3, so 2W+3 = 50 → W = 23.5 (5 yrs ago) → W now = 28.5. ODD numbers — minor inconsistency in problem typical. PYQ FREQUENCY: family-age tricky problems 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: If 6 years subtracted from PRESENT AGE of Naveen and remainder is divided by 18, we get the age of his grandson Krish, who is 2 years old. The present age of Naveen is:
questions.explanation: Let Naveen's present age = x. Per question: (x − 6) / 18 = 2 (Krish's age). Solve: x − 6 = 36 → x = 42. So Naveen is 42 years old. CHECK: (42 − 6)/18 = 36/18 = 2 ✓. KEY METHOD: TRANSLATE WORDS to ALGEBRA carefully. 'X subtracted from Y' = Y − X. 'X divided by Y' = X/Y. 'Equal to / gives / we get / is' = '='. PRACTICE: (1) 'When 5 added to Q's age divided by 7 = 3' → (Q+5)/7 = 3 → Q = 16. (2) 'A's age decreased by 10 then doubled = B's age' → 2(A−10) = B. (3) 'Half of M's age plus 5 = N's age' → M/2 + 5 = N. EXAM TIP: parse the problem CAREFULLY; rewrite the verbal problem in math NOTATION before solving. RELATED INDIA-CULTURAL: family age problems often involve 3-4 generations — child, parent, grandparent. Typical age gaps in family: ~25-30 yrs per generation. PYQ FREQUENCY: word-to-algebra age problems in SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk 1× per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests reading comprehension + linear-equation setup.
